script: NBA players with TRASH ratings, but were secretly UNSTOPPABLE! in the game. If you booted up NBA two K fourteen and searched Kyle Korver's overall rating, you probably scrolled right past him because he sat down in the sixties and looked like a role player you would never bother picking. But that number on his card was lying to you. Right before this game dropped, Korver had finished the real season second in the entire league in three point shooting at around forty-six percent, and only a couple of times in his whole career had he ever dropped under forty percent from three. So the game gave him a low overall, then cranked his three point rating up into the nineties, sitting right next to Curry. But the crazy part is that his rating wasn't even the thing that made him unfair. It was the release, because Korver had one of the quickest and most forgiving jump shots in the whole game. You could run him off a screen, catch the ball with a defender flying at your face, and that shot still dropped as long as your timing was clean, which meant a player with a low overall was pure money from anywhere behind the arc. And the reason it all felt so real came down to one thing, because that same stretch of basketball, Korver set an actual NBA record by hitting a three in one hundred twenty-seven straight games. It just copied what he was already doing for real.
